questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution enforces that it is the duty of the State to apply directive principles in making laws?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 37**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 37 of the Indian Constitution States about the application of the Directive Principles.
 
• These principles aim at ensuring socio-economic justice for the people and establishing India as a Welfare State.
 
• The source of the concept of Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) is the Spanish Constitution which came from the Irish Constitution.
 
• The concept of DPSP emerged from Article 45 of the Irish Constitution.
 
• The scope of DPSP is limitless and it protects the rights of a citizen and works at a macro level.
 
• DPSP consists of all the ideals that the State should follow and keep in mind while formulating policies and enacting laws for the country.
 
• The DPSP is not enforceable by law; it is non-justiciable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 36**

 
 
• Definition of state.
 
• According to Article 36, the term state in part4 has the same meaning as in part 3 dealing with fundamental rights
 
 
 
• **Article 38**
 
 
• State to secure a social order for the promotion of the welfare of the people.
 
• By securing a social order permeated by the justice -social, economic, and political and to minimize the inequality.
 
 
 
• **Article 39****​**
 
 
• Certain principles of policy to be followed by the state.
 
• Article 39 says livelihood, common good proper distribution, prevention of concentration of wealth, equal pay equal work, health and strength of worker and children and healthy development of children.

questions.question: What are ribosomes made up of?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Proteins and RNA**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Ribosomes are made up of both proteins and RNA**
 
• These** two components combine to form two subunits – a large subunit and a small subunit **– which together make a functional ribosome.
 
• Ribosomal **RNA plays a crucial role in the ribosome's structure and function.**
 
• It **helps in catalyzing the formation of peptide bonds, acting as a ribozyme,** which is essential for protein synthesis.
 
• **Ribosomal proteins provide structural support **and aid in the proper folding of rRNA.
 
• They also assist in assembling the ribosomal subunits and facilitating their interaction with messenger RNA (mRNA) and transfer RNA (tRNA) during protein synthesis.
 
• Ribosomes are the **site of protein synthesis** in the cell.

questions.question: In ethylene (C2H4), hybridisation of carbon atoms is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** sp2**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Hybridisation is the **process of mixing atomic orbitals to form new hybrid orbitals** suitable for the pairing of electrons to form chemical bonds in valence bond theory.
 
• Ethylene is a hydrocarbon with the formula C2H4.
 
• Carbon atoms: Each carbon atom in ethylene forms three sigma bonds (two with hydrogen atoms and one with another carbon atom) and one pi bond (with the other carbon atom).
 
• The carbon atoms in ethylene undergo sp2 hybridisation, which involves the **mixing of one s orbital and two p orbitals** to form three sp2 hybrid orbitals.
 
• The sp2 hybridisation results in a trigonal planar structure with bond angles of approximately 120°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a7167c310ffa5e6cbe93ae23b46abb87298745bd97811c62e719b26c7b16ad56.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****sp3 hybridisation:** This involves the mixing of** one s orbital and three p orbitals** to form four sp3 hybrid orbitals, which is seen in methane (CH4).

**sp hybridisation:** This involves the mixing of **one s orbital and one p orbital** to form two sp hybrid orbitals, which is seen in acetylene (C2H2).

**sp3d hybridisation:** This involves the mixing of **one s orbital, three p orbitals, and one d orbital** to form five sp3d hybrid orbitals, which is seen in molecules with trigonal bipyramidal geometry, such as phosphorus pentachloride (PCl5).

questions.question: For the first time in the country, which of the following State Governments has implemented a policy for blindness control with the objective of 'Right to Sight'?
questions.solution:

__
 
• Rajasthan is the first state in India to implement a policy specifically aimed at blindness control.
 
• The policy is named** ‘Right to Sight’**.
 
• The policy includes measures for** prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation of blindness.**
 
• The policy was launched in **January 2023**. The policy aims to reduce the prevalence rate of blindness from** 1.1% in 2020 to 0.3%** through various measures such as** keratoplasty centers** for cornea transplants, eye banks in medical colleges, and public **awareness campaigns**.

• **Tamil Nadu **was the first state in India to implement the** ‘Midday Meal Scheme’ in 1956**, which aimed to improve nutritional status and school attendance among children.

questions.question: What is the root-like structure at the base of an algae (seaweed) that binds the algae to a hard substrate like a stone?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Holdfast**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **root-like structure at the base of an alga that binds** it to a hard substrate like a **stone is called the holdfast.**
 
• The holdfast is similar to a plant root in that it anchors the organism in place.
 
• However, unlike plant roots, the holdfast's sole function is attachment and it does not extract nutrients.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Some other parts of a seaweed**:

 
 
• **Stipe**: The stalk of seaweed between the holdfast and blade, which resembles a stem
 
• **Frond:** The term used to refer to the stipe and blade together 
 
• Seaweeds are often found in dense growths on rocky shores or in shallow water.
 
• They are commercially important to humans and are used as fertilizers or as sources of polysaccharides
 
• The **midrib is the central vein of a leaf** that runs from the leaf base to the tip.

• The **73rd Amendment Act of 1992** provides for a 3-tier system of Panchayati Raj for all states having a population of **above 20 lakhs (2 million)**.

• “Village” means a village specified by the Governor by public notification to be a village for the purposes of this Part and includes a group of villages so specified.

questions.question: The battle of Khanwa was fought between the forces of the Babur and the Rajput forces led by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rana Sanga**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Battle of Khanwa was fought in 1527 between the Mughal Emperor Babur and the Rajput forces led by Rana Sanga of Mewar.**
 
• It** was a significant battle that marked the consolidation of Mughal power in India.**
 
• Babur, the founder of the Mughal Empire, led the Mughal forces, while Rana Sanga, the ruler of Mewar, led the Rajput confederacy.
 
• **The battle was triggered by Babur's desire to expand his empire **and control the fertile plains of North India.
 
• Rana Sanga,** as the leading Rajput ruler, opposed Babur's ambitions and formed a confederacy of Rajput states to resist Mughal expansion.**
 
• The **battle took place on March 17, 1527,** near the town of Khanwa in Rajasthan.
 
• Babur employed innovative military tactics, including the use of artillery and the "chakar-i-barbar" (the "whirlwind" formation), to defeat the Rajput forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ibrahim Lodi:
 
 
• Ibrahim Lodi was the last ruler of the Lodi dynasty, which ruled Delhi and parts of North India before the arrival of the Mughals.
 
• Ibrahim Lodi clashed with Babur over territorial disputes, leading to the First Battle of Panipat in 1526, where Babur defeated Lodi and established Mughal rule in North India.
 
 
 
• Medini Rai:
 
 
• Medini Rai was a Rajput ruler of Chanderi, a state in central India.
 
• He joined Rana Sanga's confederacy against Babur but was defeated and killed in the Battle of Khanwa
 
 
 
• Mahmud Lodi
 
 
• Mahmud Lodi was the second ruler of the Lodi dynasty, which ruled Delhi and parts of North India from 1451 to 1526.
 
• He succeeded his father, Bahlol Lodi, and reigned from 1489 to 1517.

questions.question: Which geostationary weather satellite launched by the European Space Agency in 1977 that provides weather imaging of Earth at both visible light and infrared wavelengths?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Meteosat.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Meteosat-1 (also known as Meteosat), was the first in the Meteosat series of geostationary weather satellites launched by the European Space Agency (ESA).
 
• It aimed to improve weather forecasting and climate research particularly for Europe and Africa.
 
• The satellite has Visible and Infrared Spin-Scan Radiometer (VISSR), allowing to capture images of the Earth's surface and atmosphere in both the visible light spectrum and infrared wavelengths.
 
• It enables 24-hour observation useful for tracking cloud cover and other weather phenomena even at night.

questions.question: The Dang Darbar Fair is held every year in which Indian state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Dangs Festival.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• Celebrated few days before Holi, Dang Darbar is an important Tribe festival of Gujarat.
 
• The Tribal festival is commemorated to honour the forefathers of the five kings of Gadhavi, Pimpri, Amala-Linga, Vasurana, and Daher.
 
• At this festival, all the five kings receive pensions from the state government.
 
• Festival tradition is believed to be 150 years old, even after independence the festival continued, though in 1954 the privileges of the kings and naiks were canceled and instead hereditary political pension was granted to them.
 
• At the festival, tourists can find stalls exhibiting art and craft items made by tribal people.
 
• Also, visitors will get a chance to see various Tribal dance forms.
 
• It is that time of the year when all the trials from the adjacent districts get down to Dang to celebrate, drink and make merry.

questions.question: Which of the following states is the least populated according to census 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arunachal Pradesh**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the 2011 census, Arunachal Pradesh is the least populated state in India. 
 
• Arunachal Pradesh is a mountainous state located in the northeastern part of India, bordering China, Myanmar, and Bhutan.
 
• Its rugged terrain and remote location have hindered population growth and development.
 
• Much of Arunachal Pradesh is covered by dense forests and mountainous regions, which are not suitable for large-scale settlement.
 
• This has led to a low population density in many parts of the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The population density is defined as the number of persons per sq km. 
 
• It is one of the important indices of population concentration.
 
• The population density of India in 2011 was 382 per sq km.
 
• Population Density of India's state as per census 2011:-

 
• NCT of Delhi - 11320.
 
• Chandigarh - 9258.
 
• Puducherry -2547.

 
• **Odisha:** Odisha is a relatively large state with a significant population.
 
• **Kerala:** Kerala is known for its high population density and literacy rate.
 
• **Andhra Pradesh:** Andhra Pradesh is another large state with a substantial population.

questions.question: How many state Legislative Council members are elected by graduates of three years standing and residing within the state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is1/12th

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 

 
• 

 

 
• 

 
• **Composition of Legislative Councils:** 
 
• State Legislative Councils in India have a total of 12th members.
 
• These members are elected through various methods, including:
 
 
• 1/3rd by members of local bodies (municipalities, gram panchayats, etc.) 
 
• 1/3rd by members of the State Legislative Assembly
 
• 1/12th by graduates of three years standing residing within the state 
 
• 1/12th by teachers of three years standing in the state
 
• 1/6th nominated by the Governor
 
 
 
• **Electoral Method:**
 
 
• The members elected by graduates are chosen through a special electoral process where only graduates with at least three years of standing within the state are eligible to vote.
 
 
 
• Therefore, 1/12th of the total members in a State Legislative Council are elected by graduates of three years standing residing within the state.
